summary: Orpheus Media - sudden session token loss during traffic surge causing truncated streaming and transient billing discrepancies
description: Issue summary: During a sustained traffic spike on 2026-03-08 02:14 UTC Orpheus Media began seeing truncated streaming responses followed by session errors (401/invalid token) and a small set of unexpectedly billed retry completions. Impact: Live chat widget truncation for a subset (~7%) of user sessions in us-east-1, elevated 5xxs and token errors for Orpheus API keys, and a measured billing delta for requests that retried after token refresh failures. Timeline (high level): - 02:12 UTC: Orpheus reports first truncated stream in #support channel. - 02:14 UTC: Support triages -> escalates to SRE; incident declared. - 02:18 UTC: Initial mitigation (circuit limiting) applied at API gateway. - 02:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis formed (session-store eviction race with KV-cache TTL bump). - 03:05 UTC: Hotfix deployed to session-store (atomic update and TTL alignment). - 03:22 UTC: Service stabilized and streaming resumes for most traffic. - 03:40 UTC: Billing review shows a small batch of duplicated completions from client-side retry loops; credits issued. Environment: prod us-east-1, Canary: none (customer on enterprise plan with dedicated routing). Steps to reproduce (attempts): 1) Replay a synthetic surge matching Orpheus traffic profile against their API key with concurrent streaming clients. 2) Force session-store TTL to roll over while concurrent requests are in-flight. 3) Observe streaming cut and subsequent 401s on reconnect attempt. Observed logs / key artifacts: - api-gateway logs: repeated "token validation failed: missing session" traces correlated with spike window. - session-store metrics: sudden TTL eviction spikes at 02:14:12 UTC. - serving-runtime traces: streaming chunk checkpoint shows truncation where backend returned EOF mid-chunk. - billing ledger snapshot: handful of completions marked as retries with distinct request_ids and same session_id. Attachments: links to dashboards (Grafana, Kibana) included in related_confluence_pages.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token refresh race causing ephemeral missing session keys in KV-store under surge.

Reproduced locally with a synthetic surge harness using Orpheus's concurrency profile; observed identical TTL eviction behavior when the session-store TTL refresh loop conflicted with garbage collection under load.

Tracing revealed that some in-flight stream handlers called token-refresh path after the session TTL had been evicted; client retry loop attempted reconnection which produced duplicate completions billed separately.

Root cause: session-store TTL refresh path performed non-atomic read-modify-write against cache; under high concurrency the GC path could evict a key between read and write windows (race). Secondary factor: a recent cache config change (TTL bump roll-out) widened the window for the race during heavy churn.

Metrics: session-store eviction rate increased by 420% during spike; 5xx rate for affected API keys rose to 6.3% (baseline 0.1%). Billing delta: approximately 0.14% of daily token volume for Orpheus (isolated batch).
Related signals: correlation with a feature flag rollout that adjusted KV-cache sync interval on 2026-03-07 21:00 UTC. Linked PR for the config change: https://github.com/redwood/config/pull/678
Reviewed recent releases: no serving-runtime kernel changes implicated; change set limited to cache sync parameters.
resolution: Applied hotfix (02:48 UTC) to session-store: convert TTL refresh to atomic upsert and add short backoff on contention. Deployed as emergency patch to prod us-east-1.
Rolled back the TTL-bump config to previous value while we validated the atomic upsert under load.
Added API gateway soft-circuit limiting to reduce concurrent refresh attempts per session_id during bursts.
Billing remediation: issued a credit equal to duplicated completions for Orpheus for the affected window; finance ticket created for manual audit (FIN-2026-0310-01).
Customer communication: sent incident summary and credits on 2026-03-09; scheduled a conference call for 2026-03-11 to review postmortem and action items.
postincident_actions: (P0) Replace non-atomic TTL refresh with atomic update in session-store (complete).
(P1) Add telemetry to surface TTL-refresh contention metrics and expose in Console per-tenant dashboard (owner: Observability team) - target 2026-03-28.
(P1) Update runbook playbook for session eviction spikes with recommended mitigation steps (circuit limits and transient backoff) - runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/93.
(P2) Add integration test that simulates KV eviction race under surge as part of CI for session-store component.
(P3) Revisit cache sync interval rollout gating for config changes; add canary and staged ramp to avoid wide TTL-window shifts.
(P2) Schedule follow-up with Orpheus CSM and Engineering to validate production behavior after config re-rollout (2026-03-25).
